chapter: Hampton, New York and Lee's own band
title: Sunday jam sessions at the Trouville
summary: Each Sunday the Nat Cole trio and Lee backed tenor, alto and trumpet players in sessions that Lee says Los Angeles started.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: But now the Trouville was where they had the best sessions - jam sessions - they ever had in Los Angeles. What we used to do at the Trouville -- the rhythm section was always Nat; you know, the trio and myself, most of the time. That was then, like, one Sunday, we had Lester, Ben, Bumps, and I don't know whether it was Don Bias or whoever, but we had the 4 tenor players. And the next Sunday, we had Willie Smith, Johnny Hodges, and 2 other alto players. And then

we had -- we'd always have the rhythm section but there would be a trumpet there; they would have Lloyd Reese, Rex Stewart, and Red Mack, who was a real good trumpet player here in town; Red Mack -- and someone else.

But that went on and on and on, and they had jam sessions every Sunday. Now, this is something a lot of people you know, were not aware of in Los Angeles, but Los Angeles really started them. As a matter of fact, that's how the Jazz at the Philharmonic became ...
